notes: Summary: Mid-market B2B SaaS (product analytics platform) looking to move from Hosted API trial to Dedicated for predictable latency and cost.
Trial feedback: Hosted API easy to integrate; streaming and function-calling worked. Observed tail-latency during peak synthetic load.
- avg daily requests: ~18k (varies by day; peak day 46k)
- token profile: avg 160 tokens/request; 60% generation/chat, 30% embeddings, 10% reranking
- observed QPS peaks: 6-9 sustained during business hours; short spikes to 14 for 1-2 minutes
- P50 latency target: <120ms for chat-turns; P95 <300ms
- Throughput: expect initial steady QPS 5-10, scale to 20 QPS over 6 months
- Concurrency planning: concurrency target 30-70 in peak windows (based on session lengths)
Model preferences: prefer open-model variants with good latency/cost tradeoff; interested in Redwood recommendations for quantized variants and fallback to smaller models for non-critical traffic
Cost sensitivity: unit-cost important; wants guidance on batching + caching policy to reduce token spend; asked for examples of expected $/1M tokens on Dedicated vs Hosted
Security: must pass SOC2 + SSO (SAML) + audit logs + KMS; data residency (US) desirable but not strict yet
Quotes / paraphrases from product lead: 'Need predictable tail latency more than lowest price. If Dedicated gives consistent p95, we'll contract.'
Internal ask: Provide capacity-sizing worksheet (QPS x concurrency x token mix) and 2 pricing options: Reserved (12-month commit) and On-demand burst
POC idea: run 2-week Dedicated pilot for one customer-facing product line (chat + search) to benchmark p95 and cost delta
Notes about integration: uses React frontend + Go backend; currently calling Redwood via SDK server-side; embeddings used for similarity search in vector DB (we store vectors in-house)
Risk: legal wants clarity on retention controls and ability to purge logs for certain customers
